_comment: Provenance manifest for the official GKS guideline PDFs that feed the official
knowledge layer. Ingestion reads ONLY the local `path` below -- it never downloads
at build time -- and refuses to run if a file's sha256 no longer matches, so a
changed or swapped PDF can never be ingested silently.
`active`: true  = ingested into the index and retrievable by the assistant.
false = kept for version history / audit ONLY. Still hash-verified on
every build so the archived copy can't drift, but never ingested,
so it can never surface as official evidence.
Superseded editions must stay archived rather than being deleted: they are the
record of what an applicant was told at the time, and `superseded_by` keeps the
To check whether NIIED/the publisher has changed a document since it was captured:
Refreshing a source is a deliberate, reviewed action: download the new file, verify
it by hand, then update `sha256`, `retrieved_at` and `cycle` here in the same commit.

sources.title: GKS-U 2026 Application Guidelines (Revised)
sources.notes: The sole active 2026 UG source. Already committed to KMate before the RAG work (see lib/official-guidelines.ts); origin_url unknown, mirrored locally. Issued after the October 2025 NIRS fire took the Study in Korea portal offline; this is the edition that actually governed the cycle.

sources.title: GKS-U 2026 Application Guidelines (Original)
sources.excluded_reason: Superseded. Retained for version history and audit only, never ingested. It directly contradicts the active revision on facts an applicant would act on -- Embassy Track deadline (Sept 30 vs Oct 17), first-round result dates (Oct 17/Nov 14 vs Oct 27/Nov 21), submission method (online via Study in Korea vs direct to embassy/university), document counts, and the Evaluation Preference list (7 items vs 5). Indexing both would let retrieval answer with a rule that was withdrawn.
sources.notes: Still surfaced to users in KMate's Official Guidelines page (lib/official-guidelines.ts) with a 'what changed' note -- that is a deliberate transparency feature and is separate from RAG retrieval.
